migration.description: Persist the single configured execution host enrollment, revocable Connector credentials, active connection generation and bounded reconnect cursors per session and run stream.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one Host Gateway candidate; migration 00007 must be present before the ordered application migration chain is applied.

durable_state.description: The one installation host registration owns its deployment credentials and current online state, while bounded Connector event cursors are keyed by session and run stream. At most one generation is active per host; stale generations cannot update state.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables managed by the embedded Goose application migration history.

source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one Host Gateway candidate containing migration 00008.
source_compatibility_range.earlier_state: The missing host tables are treated as an unapplied migration; no earlier Host Gateway state is interpreted by the runtime. The complete application chain remains ordered behind migration 00007.

ordered_operations.description: Create the singleton host_registrations row with online state and connection generation.
Create host_credentials with one-way token hashes and revocation timestamps.
Create host_connections with one active credential and generation per host.
Create host_cursors keyed by host, session and run stream with bounded retention.

rollout_signals: Goose records migration 00008 only after the parent-owned migration 00007 is available in the complete chain.
Connector authentication accepts only an unrevoked hash; registration is singleton-scoped and connection state changes require the current host generation.
Cursor checkpoints carry an explicit retention deadline, are keyed by their owning host/session/run stream and are processed under the current generation.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version-or-a-compatible switchback only when the current state remains readable

validation: A registration returns a raw Connector credential once, stores only its SHA-256 hash, and a revoked credential cannot authenticate a new connection.
Opening a replacement connection increments the host generation; stale heartbeats, cursor writes and closes do not change the replacement connection's state.
Each stream cursor survives database close and reopen, is scoped to its host/session/run key, and is not resumed after its configured retention deadline.
Re-running migration discovery leaves the four tables, singleton constraint, indexes and migration history unchanged.
